summary: Tested the fix for vague error messages in wizard pages. Backend test-connection endpoints now return structured 'steps' arrays instead of 'suggestion' strings. Frontend DomainManager.js wizard shows detailed step-by-step instructions for Cloudflare API Token and Zone ID setup. ConnectionStatus.js component renders steps as numbered lists with 'How to fix this:' header.

issues: DialogContent missing DialogTitle for accessibility (console warning from Radix UI) - pre-existing issue

context_for_next_testing_agent: All test-connection endpoints now return {status, message, steps[], link?, link_label?} format instead of {status, message, suggestion}. The ConnectionStatus.js component renders steps as numbered lists with 'How to fix this:' header and orange accent. DomainManager.js Cloudflare wizard shows 6-step instructions for API Token and 5-step instructions for Zone ID.

steps: Go to dash.cloudflare.com and log in
Click your profile icon (top right) → My Profile
Click 'API Tokens' in the left sidebar
Click 'Create Token' → use the 'Edit zone DNS' template
Copy the token and paste it in Step 1 above
Your credentials are valid but your account lacks the required permissions
Contact Radioplayer support to verify your account has 'Now Playing' push access
Make sure your station is active and approved on the Radioplayer platform
Go to canva.com/developers and log in with your Canva account
Create a new app (or open your existing app)
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
Paste them in Step 1 of this wizard
Open the VMix Director page to auto-create a default configuration
Then come back here and test the connection again

cloudflare_step1_api_token.header: HOW TO CREATE YOUR CLOUDFLARE API TOKEN:
steps_verified: Find the template 'Edit zone DNS' and click 'Use template'
Under 'Zone Resources', select your domain (e.g. koodh.com)
Copy the token and paste it below
cloudflare_step1_api_token.important_note: This is an API Token, not your Cloudflare password or Global API Key

cloudflare_step2_zone_id.header: HOW TO FIND YOUR ZONE ID:
steps_verified: Click on your domain name (e.g. koodh.com)
On the Overview page, scroll down on the right sidebar
Find 'Zone ID' under the 'API' section — it looks like a1b2c3d4e5f6...
Copy it and paste it below

features_verified: Shows 'How to fix this:' header with amber/orange accent
Falls back to 'suggestion' string for legacy responses
